summary: AE + SE ran a detailed POC scoping focused on open-model options for a clinical summarization/triage use case. Discussed success criteria (latency <300ms p95, >92% clinical accuracy on test set, throughput 120 qps peak), workload sizing, benchmark plan, timeline (2-4 week POC), and security constraints (PHI, HIPAA, VPC, KMS). Shortlist: Llama 3 70B (quantized), Mistral Instruct, Falcon-180B-instruct (quantized), and a domain-tuned Vicuna variant; discussed tradeoffs between latency/cost/accuracy and multilingual needs (English + Spanish). Next steps: share benchmark plan & prompts, customer to provide de-identified dataset, schedule dedicated throughput run and security Q/A.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-09
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Sofia Martinez, Ankit Rao, Maya Chen (Redwood); Dr. Priya Shah, Rahul Mehta, Emily Carter, Marcus Lane, Nora Patel (AegisHealth)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): quick run through POC goals, shortlist of open models, benchmark plan and timeline, security constraints - PHI and VPC, next steps for dataset and tests

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Alright team, thanks for joining. Uh, I'm Jordan, AE on the account, with Sofia and Ankit from solutions eng. Maya from CS. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dr. Priya Shah: Doing well, thanks. We've been waiting to nail down the model selection and the POC success criteria.
[00:13] Jordan Lee: Perfect, that's exactly what we want to go through. Quick agenda — success criteria, workload profile, bench plan, timeline, security. Then we'll propose a shortlist of open-models and tradeoffs. Sound good?
[00:22] Rahul Mehta: Yes. Also want to make sure we cover PHI controls and the option for a private deployment.
[00:26] Sofia Martinez: Absolutely. We'll cover hosted vs dedicated vs private and what we recommend for a PHI-sensitive triage/summarization workload.

[02:01] Ankit Rao: To kick off — can you confirm the core POC use case? My notes say: clinical note summarization + triage suggestions to route to specialty queues. Is that right?
[02:10] Nora Patel: Yes, and multilingual support, English and Spanish primarily. We also want entity extraction/concept tagging to feed downstream analytics.
[02:18] Emily Carter: We're not sending raw PHI to any 3rd party unless we have BAA and private networking in place — that's a hard requirement.

[03:05] Jordan Lee: Understood. On success metrics, what are you prioritizing? Accuracy vs latency vs cost?
[03:12] Dr. Priya Shah: Clinical accuracy is top. We need at least 92% on our labeled test set for critical fields and <5% hallucination on med facts. Latency is second — p95 ideally <300ms for single note summarization when under normal load, but we can tolerate slightly higher for batch. Cost is lower priority but still important for scale.
[03:33] Marcus Lane: Security: HIPAA compliance, audit logs, KMS integration, and ability to run inside our VPC or on-prem with private control plane.

[04:45] Sofia Martinez: Great, those are actionable. For workload sizing — can you confirm QPS and average tokens per request?
[04:52] Emily Carter: Peak user-facing QPS estimated at 120 qps during business hours, avg payload size ~1.2k tokens, worst-case up to 3k tokens for longer notes. Throughput for batch jobs at night maybe 5k notes/hour.
[05:08] Ankit Rao: So we need both low-latency single-note paths and high-throughput batch paths. That maps to potentially different model/quantization profiles.

[06:20] Jordan Lee: On benchmarking: we'll propose two benchmark tracks — 1) latency/throughput microbench on your infra or our dedicated, 2) quality evals on your labeled holdout with the prompt set. The quality eval will include hallucination checks and clinical field accuracy.
[06:38] Dr. Priya Shah: For quality eval we will share a de-identified 500-record holdout and a 2k prompt set for robustness testing.
[06:46] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Timeline-wise, what's your target for POC completion?
[06:50] Rahul Mehta: Ideally 3 weeks to demo to product leadership, 6-8 weeks max for a fuller evaluation.
[06:57] Sofia Martinez: We typically run a 2-4 week POC depending on benchmarks — initial quality pass in week 1-2, throughput runs in week 2-3. Sounds like your timeline aligns.

[08:10] Ankit Rao: Let's talk model shortlist. Given domain sensitivity and multilingual needs, our recommended open models to test: Llama 3 70B (q8_0 / quantized), Mistral-Instruct 7B/our tuned 7B variant, Falcon-180B-instruct quantized, and a domain-adapted Vicuna 13B variant that other medical teams often spin up. We'll also test a distilled Mistral for latency.
[08:37] Dr. Priya Shah: Why Llama 3 70B vs smaller models? Concerned about latency/cost if we pick 70B.
[08:42] Sofia Martinez: Right — tradeoffs: Llama 3 70B tends to have stronger instruction following and fewer omissions on medical summaries, so quality is higher. But quantized 70B still costs more GPU and has higher latency than 7-13B. We suggested quantization and kernel tuning; on A100/V100 families we can get p95 under 300ms for single-turn with aggressive batching and KV cache reuse for similar notes, but it depends on hardware.
[09:07] Marcus Lane: Is there a difference in on-prem compatibility?
[09:10] Ankit Rao: All of these can run in private deployments. For Falcon-180B you'll want adequate GPU memory (80GB+ or sharded across nodes) — that increases ops complexity. Mistral 7B variants are easiest to host and cheapest, with best latency.

[10:00] Jordan Lee: For multilingual, Mistral and Llama 3 handle Spanish reasonably well; domain tuning on your de-id clinical notes will improve Latinx/Spanish idioms. Vicuna variants that were fine-tuned on clinical corpora might give a boost on entity extraction.

[11:12] Dr. Priya Shah: If we emphasize accuracy, seems like Llama3 70B or Falcon would be winners, but cost is a worry.
[11:18] Sofia Martinez: Exactly. So POC approach: run parallel quality tests across the shortlist and a latency sweep. We'll present a cost/accuracy curve. For production, if cost dominates, a quantized 13B or tuned 7B might be the sweet spot.

[12:42] Emily Carter: On data flow: we will provide de-identified notes via S3 in our account. We need Redwood to run the quality evals inside our VPC or with a Private deployment due to PHI. Is that feasible?
[12:55] Maya Chen: Yes, we can run the POC in Redwood Dedicated inside a private VPC or an on-prem package if needed. We have a Private deployment offering with a customer-managed control plane. For immediate benching we can also do a short dedicated instance with BAA in place.
[13:20] Marcus Lane: We'll need KMS integration and access logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also ask about key rotation and HSM support.
[13:29] Ankit Rao: We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can expose audit logs and CloudTrail style events. HSM options are available in Private. We'll put the security brief in the follow-up doc.

[14:40] Jordan Lee: Back to benchmarks — Sofia, can you outline the benchmark plan quick?
[14:46] Sofia Martinez: Sure. Two parallel tracks: Quality track: run each model on the 500-record holdout, metrics: field accuracy, F1 for entity extraction, hallucination rate. We'll run prompts with temperature sweeps and a couple of instruction formats. Latency/throughput track: run single-turn latency p50/p95 on representative infra, then scale to 120 qps peak using batching and concurrency tests; measure token/sec and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also do a dedicated throughput run using Redwood Dedicated to demonstrate end-to-end.
[15:22] Nora Patel: What's the expected time to get quality results?
[15:26] Sofia Martinez: For 4 models on 500 records, we can run within 48 hours after we receive data and prompt set, results in 3 calendar days including analysis. Throughput runs usually take 2-3 days to set up and run depending on VPC provisioning.

[16:40] Rahul Mehta: For the throughput test — do you simulate user concurrency or replay real traffic?
[16:45] Ankit Rao: We can do both. Replay a traffic CSV you provide or simulate user pattern. We recommend replaying a 1-week sample to exercise tails.

[18:10] Dr. Priya Shah: On hallucination measurement, what's your methodology?
[18:14] Sofia Martinez: We do a combination of automated checks (entity mismatch detection), and a manual spot-check by clinicians on flagged responses. We'll surface the false-positive/false-negative types. We will also include a confidence score calibration test.

[20:00] Jordan Lee: Cost modeling — we'll produce estimated per-1k token costs across models and quant levels. That'll feed into your total cost projection.
[20:08] Emily Carter: Are the quantized Llama 3 weights you mentioned compatible with our target infra? We run on A100s.
[20:13] Ankit Rao: Yes, A100 is good. For 70B quantized you'll likely need 2x80GB per replica or sharded solution. We can run optimized kernels to lower memory and latency. We'll include recommended infra profiles.

[22:30] Marcus Lane: On compliance paperwork, do you have a SOC2 report and BAA template to start?
[22:36] Maya Chen: Yes, we will share SOC2 Type II attestation and a standard BAA template in the follow-up packet. We'll also include our security architecture doc and audit log examples.

[24:05] Nora Patel: Are there any OpenAI/Anthropic style fallbacks we should worry about? Meaning, do you offer fallback to hosted models if capacity spikes?
[24:13] Jordan Lee: We support smart routing and fallback policies. For POC we'll keep traffic in your Dedicated or Private environment, but as an option we can show fallback to a hosted smaller model. We'll surface the SLA differences.

[25:40] Dr. Priya Shah: For multilingual behavior — do you recommend fine-tuning or translation + model?
[25:46] Sofia Martinez: If Spanish is common and domain-specific, a small domain-adaptive fine-tune or LoRA is recommended. Alternatively, you can run an initial pass with the same model and then apply a bilingual fine-tune; we'll test both in POC. Fine-tune improves idiomatic handling and entity extraction.

[27:00] Ankit Rao: Quick note on safety guardrails — we'll include a safety schema and content filters, plus redaction heuristics for PII/PHI in post-processing. That's part of our standard POC checklist.

[28:30] Emily Carter: How do we compare Mistral vs Vicuna for entity extraction specifically?
[28:35] Sofia Martinez: Mistral-Instruct tends to be stronger on instruction following for short prompts; Vicuna variants that were fine-tuned on instruction data and clinical corpora can outperform on entity extraction after tuning. We'll benchmark both.

[30:00] Jordan Lee: Let's agree on the shortlist now: Llama 3 70B quantized, Falcon-180B-instruct (quantized) for quality ceiling, Mistral-Instruct 7B (and distilled 7B) for latency/cost baseline, and a Vicuna 13B clinical-tuned variant for domain lift. Any objections?
[30:17] Rahul Mehta: No objections — sounds comprehensive.
[30:20] Marcus Lane: Make sure you document operational complexity for Falcon 180B — we need clear runbooks.
[30:26] Ankit Rao: We'll provide runbooks and sharding guidance.

[32:15] Nora Patel: On success criteria recap: 92% field accuracy, hallucination <5%, p95 latency <300ms for single note under typical load, sustained throughput to 120 qps with acceptable degradation. Agreed?
[32:30] Dr. Priya Shah: Yes, and ability to run in Private with KMS and audit logs.
[32:35] Jordan Lee: Agreed. We'll tie those to pass/fail thresholds in the benchmark report.

[34:00] Emily Carter: Any blockers on our side before you can start? We'll need to anonymize the sample and get legal to sign BAA.
[34:07] Maya Chen: BAA and de-id data are the two prerequisites. Also ask that you share a small dev VPC CIDR so we can provision networking.

[35:18] Jordan Lee: Next steps recap: Jordan sends shortlist + benchmark plan + pricing by Wed (2027-05-12). Sofia sends prompt templates and test harness. Emily shares de-id dataset and traffic CSV by 2027-05-14. Marcus to provide compliance checklist by 2027-05-11. We'll then schedule the dedicated throughput run week of 2027-05-17.

[36:10] Dr. Priya Shah: Timeline sounds good. One more question — will the POC include any tuning (LoRA/fine-tune) inside the 2-4 week window?
[36:18] Sofia Martinez: Baseline quality tests first. If tuning looks promising, we can run a small LoRA adapt within the POC (adds about 3-5 days) — we'll surface tradeoffs in the plan.

[38:05] Marcus Lane: For the security doc, please include incident response contacts and data retention specifics.
[38:11] Maya Chen: We'll include that.

[39:22] Jordan Lee: Anything else from the customer?
[39:26] Nora Patel: No, thank you. We appreciate the thoroughness.
[39:30] Rahul Mehta: Thanks, team. Looking forward to the plan.

[40:00] Jordan Lee: Great. We'll follow up with the packet. Meeting end.

Notes/References mentioned:
